q: Which Burgundy house was moved by the 1979 'Wine Olympics' upset to buy land in the Dundee Hills in 1987?
ans: Maison Joseph Drouhin (1987; Véronique Drouhin winemaking)
exp: In Drouhin's 1980 rematch his own Chambolle-Musigny edged Eyrie's 1975 South Block by a fraction — close enough to send him to Oregon.

q: The Missoula Floods matter to Washington wine because they:
accept: deposited the gravel and silt soils
ice age floods laid the soils
ans: Laid the gravels, sands and silts over Columbia basalt that vines now root in
exp: Ice-age megafloods swept the basin ~15,000 years ago; loess blew in above.

q: Red Mountain's reputation rests on which style?
exp: Hot, windy, southwest-facing: Quilceda Creek and Col Solare fruit sources. Red Mountain is Washington's most tannic and concentrated Cabernet source.

q: The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater gives Syrah a signature best described as:
ans: Savory, olive-tapenade, umami 'Rocks funk' from basalt cobblestones
exp: Cayuse (Christophe Baron) planted it 1997; geologically the AVA sits in Oregon, commercially with Walla Walla.

q: Chateau Ste. Michelle's long Riesling collaboration with Ernst Loosen is labeled:
exp: It re-anchored Washington as the New World's Riesling volume leader.

q: Dr. Konstantin Frank's 1962 breakthrough in the Finger Lakes proved:
accept: vinifera could survive cold climates grafted
european vines viable in new york
ans: That grafted vinifera could survive Finger Lakes winters — against the hybrid orthodoxy
exp: A Ukrainian-born PhD washing dishes at Geneva station until Charles Fournier listened.

q: Which two deep lakes moderate the core Finger Lakes vineyards?
ans: Seneca and Cayuga (Keuka the historic third)
exp: Seneca rarely freezes — 'the banana belt' hugs its shores.

q: VQA Icewine rules require harvest at what temperature and forbid what?
ans: −8°C or colder on the vine; artificial freezing (cryoextraction) prohibited
exp: Ontario's Niagara Peninsula is the volume king; Inniskillin's 1989 Vidal won Vinexpo's Grand Prix.

q: British Columbia's dominant fine-wine valley, an arid lake-moderated trench, is:
exp: Desert north of 49°: Syrah and Bordeaux reds south, Pinot and Riesling north; Similkameen beside it.

q: Name Washington's first AVA and its year.
exp: Columbia Valley followed in 1984 as the umbrella.

q: Which Oregon AVA is the smallest, nested entirely inside the Chehalem Mountains AVA?
exp: A single geological formation of marine sedimentary Willakenzie soils.

q: Explain the Laurelwood District AVA's defining soil.
ans: Laurelwood soil — windblown loess over ancient basalt, on the Chehalem Mountains' northeast flank
exp: Established 2020; loess gives a distinctly silkier tannin.

q: Which vinifera grape leads plantings in the Finger Lakes?
exp: Riesling is the region's identity and its best argument.

q: Name Canada's four wine provinces with their own appellation systems.
accept: ontario british columbia quebec nova scotia
ans: Ontario, British Columbia, Québec, Nova Scotia
exp: Ontario and BC produce the overwhelming majority.

q: Explain the Niagara Escarpment's role in Ontario viticulture.
accept: air circulation lake effect moderation slope
ans: It channels lake-moderated air over the vineyards, extending the season and buffering winter kill
exp: The Beamsville Bench sub-appellation sits on its slope.

q: Which AVA holds Long Island's serious vineyard concentration, and which red grape is its benchmark?
accept: north fork of long island merlot
north fork of long island and merlot is the benchmark red
merlot on the north fork of long island
ans: North Fork of Long Island (1986) — Merlot; The Hamptons/Long Island (1985) and the umbrella Long Island AVA (2001) complete the set
exp: Hargrave Vineyard planted the first vinifera here in 1973, on a former potato farm. The Atlantic gives the North Fork one of the East's longest and latest growing seasons — a genuinely maritime, Bordeaux-shaped climate with little winter kill — and also its worst problem, September humidity, rot and hurricanes. That is why the region settled on Merlot and Cabernet Franc rather than Cabernet Sauvignon, which too often fails to finish before the weather turns. Note the chronology trap: The Hamptons was approved first, but the North Fork carries the plantings.
